raw_response:
I’m 67 this year, and I’ve worked these fields my whole life. For wheat and maize, I still follow the wheat-maize cycle because on a small place like mine, that is the safest way to keep grain coming and not leave land idle. I only have 10.1 mu, and some people in the house work outside, so I cannot make things too fancy or too labor-heavy. I finished last year seeing wheat did alright when I gave enough base fertilizer and watered at the key times, so I’ll keep that general way. The well water helps, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate unless the crop really needs it. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and plant quickly. Chili gives cash, but it takes more watching and more labor, so I’ll only keep a smaller area for that, enough to earn some money without tying up the whole family.

I’m not the kind to calculate everything exactly like a college expert, but after so many years I know the field and I listen when people around me do well. If wheat looks weak, I’ll topdress a bit more at jointing. If maize comes up strong and rain is decent, I won’t waste money on extra water. Chili is different: if I see insects or disease starting, I have to act fast or the whole patch suffers. This year I’ll stay steady, not take big risks, and use what has worked on my land before.
